stories.headline: Roberto De Zerbi on misfiring Tottenham: 'We are going to win many games and score many goals'
stories.summary: Roberto De Zerbi has said that when his Tottenham Hotspur team clicks, they "are going to win many games and score many goals."
stories.body:
Roberto De Zerbi has said that when his Tottenham Hotspur team clicks, he believes they "are going to win many games and score many goals."

The Spurs head coach was speaking after Spurs were knocked out of the Carabao Cup with a 3-1 loss to Liverpool on Tuesday. Four games into the new Premier League season, Tottenham are still searching for their first goal of the campaign.

Conor Gallagher's second-half header at Anfield was the first goal Spurs have scored against top-flight opposition this season.

Despite the scoreline, Tottenham did edge Liverpool on xG (2.34 vs. 1.53), possession (56% vs. 44%), shots (17 vs. 12) and shots on target (6 vs. 5) and De Zerbi said that he sees signs that things are coming together for his new-look team.

"We have to be stronger," De Zerbi said. "I think last season was a school. I think it has to be a school for everyone. Now we are unlucky, because it's clear we have to improve many, many things, but also this night we played well, we created more chances, we shot more times, we got more corners than Liverpool. We could score more goals.

"I remember six, seven clear chances to score. Lucas Bergvall, Kudus and Udogie. In the second half, a couple with Marmoush, one Sávio, one Bergvall, another corner. I can't say nothing today.

"Now, my focus is on Villa and we have to prepare our best in the next game with this mentality to find this click.

"We are suffering because the results are our life, no? If we lose, we are sorry, we are sad, we are disappointed, we are frustrated. It's tough, no? But it's the first moment, the first part of this new project. I think when we make the click... but the click is not mentality, because today we showed the right mentality, the right behaviour and we played until the end of the game. I think we are going to win many games and score many goals."

- All 20 Premier League teams ranked: Which managers will be fired first?

Tottenham host also-winless Aston Villa in north London on Saturday in their next fixture and the Spurs boss has called on his team to sharpen up in the final third.

"We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better and we have to finish better the clear situations but we are sorry for the result, disappointed, frustrated," he said.

"We have to be stronger in these unlucky moments because I am honest with myself and with you. I think this five or six games we have been for sure not lucky.

"I believe in my players, I have a big opinion of them and when we arrive to finally click to win a game we will enjoy it with these players because the look of the players is incredible.

"It is a tough moment but we have to be stronger."

stories.headline: F1 2027 calendar: Monaco GP gets sprint race, Türkiye and Portugal return to schedule
stories.summary: The 2027 Monaco Grand Prix has been named as one of 10 sprint races on next year's 24-race calendar, which includes the return of rounds in Türkiye and Portugal.
stories.body:
The 2027 Monaco Grand Prix has been named as one of 10 sprint races on next year's 24-race calendar, which includes the return of rounds in Türkiye and Portugal.

The 2027 schedule is set to get underway with a sprint race in Bahrain on March 14 and run until the final race of the season in Abu Dhabi on Dec. 12, which will also feature Formula 1's sprint format.

The addition of a sprint race in Monaco is among the most unexpected additions to the calendar as the tight street circuit is notorious for its lack of overtaking.

Sprint weekends feature just one practice session on Friday followed by sprint qualifying the same day, a sprint race (one third of the length of a full grand prix) on Saturday before the standard qualifying and the grand prix take place on Saturday and Sunday as usual.

Sources have indicated to ESPN that Formula 1 believes the addition of a second qualifying session in Monaco will add value over two practice sessions, with the potential for two different grid orders in the sprint and main grand prix.

Qualifying has long been seen as the highlight of the Monaco Grand Prix weekend, partly due to the skill required to thread a car between the narrow barriers and partly because it very often defines the finishing order for Sunday's grand prix.

F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has been keen to increase the number of sprint races in recent years due to the increased viewership the format receives by substituting two extra competitive sessions for two practice sessions.

"Data shows that total viewership of Sprint weekends is 12% higher than non-Sprint weekends, Sprint Qualifying is up to three times more popular with fans than Free Practice," F1 said in a press release. "82% of attendees at Sprint weekends say it adds value to their ticket, and 75% of F1 fans believe Sprint events add greater value to a season's calendar."

Sprint races have also been scheduled for the first round in Bahrain (March 14), the third round in Australia (April 4), the fourth round in Japan (April 11), the seventh round in Canada (May 23), the tenth round in Great Britain (July 4), the 14th round in Italy (Sept. 5), the 21st round in Brazil (Nov. 7), the 23rd round in Qatar (Dec. 5) and the 24th round in Abu Dhabi (Dec. 12).

- Verstappen on Max vs 100: 'Embarrassing' to lose

- Russell follows Hamilton in conceding title to Kimi

- Honda replacing engine chief after poor start to '26

Portugal (June 20) and Türkiye (Oct. 3) return to the calendar in 2027 while the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix and Dutch Grand Prix fall of the schedule.

The Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix is set to return in 2028 as it enters a yearly rotation with the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa-Francorchamps, while there are no plans for the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort to return.

"The 2027 calendar brings together some of the most iconic circuits and vibrant cities in the world, creating an incredible stage for another unforgettable season of Formula 1," Domenicali said. "We are thrilled to welcome Portugal and Türkiye to the championship and to expand Sprint racing to ten events, giving our fans even more intensity, drama, and the wheel-to-wheel action that make our sport so special.

President of the FIA Mohammed Ben Sulayem added: "The 2027 FIA Formula One World Championship calendar is a strong reflection of the global appeal and continued growth of our sport. With twenty-four Grands Prix across five continents, the return of Portugal and Türkiye, and the opportunity for an expanded Sprint programme, the calendar combines tradition, innovation, and fan engagement while maintaining the highest sporting standards."

The calendar, which also includes a preseason test in Bahrain from Feb. 24 to 27, has been announced despite ongoing conflict in the Middle East and uncertainty over where this year's season will end.

The final two rounds of the 2026 season are due to take place in Qatar on Nov. 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6, although Imola is being held as a back-up option if the two races cannot go ahead due to security threats linked to the war between the United States and Iran.

Earlier this year, races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, which are scheduled to hold the opening two rounds of the 2027 calendar, had to be cancelled due to the conflict. The Bahrain Grand Prix was then rescheduled to take place in Malaysia later this month.

stories.headline: Kwity Paye makes dream start to Las Vegas Raiders career in NFL opening week
stories.summary: Kwity Paye had a dream debut for the Las Vegas Raiders in one of the standout performances of the first week of the NFL.
stories.body:
Kwity Paye had a dream debut for the Las Vegas Raiders in one of the standout performances of the first week of the NFL.

Paye - a Guinea-born Liberian defensive end - earns our Africa player of the Week nod for the first week of the new NFL season. There were plenty of other stars - either from the continent directly or with directly traceable lineage - who started with a bang.

Kyle Monangai - a first-generation Cameroonian-American running back - scored a memorable touchdown for the Chicago Bears in their win over the Carolina Panthers.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba - who is of Sierra Leonean descent through his grandparents - gave a timely reminder of why he is the reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year in the Seattle Seahawks' win over the New England Patriots.

Africa Player of the Week: Kwity Paye (Las Vegas Raiders)
Paye was involved in three of the five sacks on Malik Willis in his first regular season game for the Raiders after joining from the Indianapolis Colts - ending with a personal tally of two (one sack and two split-sacks, counting for 0.5 each). He additionally notched four quarter-back hits among a total of six tackles.

The 27-year-old played an integral part in a solid defensive performance as the Raiders beat the Miami Dolphins 27-13.

Paye pinned the Dolphins back two yards with his very first tackle of the game on the first drive - made together with Taron Johnson on De'Von Achane.

His first split-sack came on the second Dolphins drive as he and Folorunso Fatukasi - who is of Nigerian descent - brought down Willis.

Paye picked up another split-sack on Willis with Maxx Crosby early in the fourth quarter to keep the lead at 14 points.

The last sack of the game on Willis - with around three minutes remaining - was all Paye's and by that stage, it was effectively the cherry on the icing, topping off a tremendous debut.

Africa Moment of the Week: Kyle Monangai (Chicago Bears)
Monangai scored a career best 61-yard running touchdown in the Bears' 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers.

While the Bears may eventually have won the game by a comfortable 22-point margin, the victory was far from settled at the time of Monangai's marauding run, which stretched the lead from seven to 14 points at the end of the third quarter.

Monangai's Cameroonian parents grew up loving soccer, but in his second season in the NFL, their son continues to excel at a different type of football.

Honorable Mentions
Jaxon Smith-Njigba gained 122 yards across eight receptions in the Seattle Seahawks' 13-10 win over the New England Patriots, picking up where he left off last season and scoring a touchdown.

Boye Mafe, the proud son of Nigerian parents, brought down Baker Mayfield and forced a fumble in the Cincinnati Bengals' 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Foyesade Oluokun, another star with ties to Nigeria, made an interception in the Jacksonville Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Cleveland Browns.

Another compatriot, Kingsley Enagbare, made a sack in the New York Jets' 23-10 over the Tennessee Titans. Elic Ayomanor, who is of Nigerian and Liberian descent, was on the losing side despite scoring a touchdown.

Chuba Hubbard, like Ayomanor, is Canadian and of Nigerian descent. He, too, was on the scoreboard in a defeat in Week 1. Hubbard scored two touchdowns in the Panthers' defeat to the Bears.

Bobby Okereke - a California-born star of proud Nigerian heritage forced a fumble despite ending up on the losing side. Nigeria-born Princely Umanmielen picked up a sack for the Panthers in defeat.

Odafe Oweh (a first-generation American of Nigerian descent and a Washington Commanders star) made a sack in the narrow 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

Donovan Ezeiruaku - also of Nigerian descent - had an impressive performance on defense for the Dallas Cowboys but also ended up on the losing side in a 28-20 defeat to the New York Giants.

Felix Anudike-Uzomah - yet another player with roots in Nigeria - made a sack for the Kansas City Chiefs in their 31-10 Monday night win over the Denver Broncos.

Africa-born Player Watch
The obvious winner among players born on the continent is Paye this week as he claims Africa Player of the Week honors even ahead of those from the diaspora not born directly in Africa.

It is not every week that the continent gets to see a performance as spectacular as Paye's, but Africa has undoubtedly advanced in the development of homegrown talent.

Paye's heroics and Umanmielen's sack for the Panthers aside, Zimbabwe's Nate Landman made eight tackles in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, though he was injured in the process.

Landman will hope to be fit for the clash against the Giants - who gave homegrown Nigerian International Player Pathway (IPP) star Basil Chijioke 'CJ' Okoye his team debut in the 28-20 win over the Cowboys.

stories.headline: Champion Hurricanes give captain Jordan Staal, 38, new deal
stories.summary: Veteran forward Jordan Staal, 38, who captained the Carolina Hurricanes to a Stanley Cup title in June, winning the Conn Smythe Trophy for postseason MVP along the way, signed a one-year contract extension with the club late Tuesday night.
stories.body:
Veteran forward Jordan Staal, who captained the Carolina Hurricanes to a Stanley Cup title in June, signed a one-year contract extension with the club Tuesday night.

Staal's deal now runs through the 2027-28 season, and it will pay a base salary of $900,000, with a $4 million signing bonus and up to $5.1 million in additional performance bonuses, the team announced in a statement.

"Jordan is not only our captain, he's the bedrock of the culture we've established in this organization," Hurricanes general manager Eric Tulsky said in the release. "His leadership, and on-ice performance throughout last season, and especially in the playoffs, was a primary factor in bringing the Stanley Cup back to Raleigh."

Staal, 38, finished the regular season with 20 goals and 36 points in 75 games, as the Hurricanes won the Metropolitan Division. He added eight goals and 12 points in 19 playoff games en route to securing the Conn Smythe Trophy as the most valuable player in the postseason.

A native of Thunder Bay, Ontario, Staal enters this season with 747 career points. He was the NHL's No. 2 pick by the Pittsburgh Penguins in 2006.

stories.headline: Cristian 'Kily' González arrives to take charge of Messi, Miami
stories.summary: New Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said he feels blessed at being given the opportunity to lead the club and coach Lionel Messi, after formerly taking up the role on Tuesday.
stories.body:
FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. -- New Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said he feels blessed at being given the opportunity to lead the club and coach Lionel Messi, after formerly taking up the role on Tuesday.

González has now received the authorization to begin the job after being announced last month as the permanent replacement for interim coach Guillermo Hoyos on a contract through June 2028.

The job sees him reunite with Messi after the two shared the field for Argentina in two World Cup qualifiers in 2005.

"There are things in football that simply cannot be described in words; they are unique feelings. I feel privileged and blessed to have this opportunity and to share the fantastic relationship I have with Leo," González said in a news conference.

"I adore him, he knows it, and that makes this moment even more special. Being with him and sharing experiences with the incredible players on this squad. Honestly, as a coach, I feel completely fulfilled.

"Of course, this is all wonderful, but now we have to get to work. God willing, we'll start off strong tomorrow and win the championship."

González led his first training session with Inter Miami on Tuesday after landing in Miami from Argentina earlier in the morning. He will be on the sidelines for the team's Campeones Cup match against Liga MX champions Cruz Azul on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.

Inter Miami reached an agreement with González on Aug. 27, but the coach could not take over for Hoyos until receiving his work permit.

"What were these past few days like? To be honest, they were filled with a lot of anticipation. It had been nearly two and a half weeks and I couldn't be here, but this unique opportunity, something I hadn't even dared to dream of, became a reality," González said.

"We spoke with the club, and they offered me the chance to join the team; I said yes immediately. Being with the players, seeing their willingness to welcome my coaching staff, and watching them train the way they did today honestly, it made me very happy and gave me a huge boost of energy for tomorrow's match."

Miami's opponent in the Campeones Cup was delayed in arriving in Miami for the game and instead of landing in the U.S. on Monday, were unable to fly in until Tuesday.

"Well, more than an odyssey, sometimes accidents like this happen, and you just have to turn the page," said Cruz Azul manager Joel Huiqui. "The team is doing well. We rested very well yesterday, we stayed at a hotel in Mexico, and we're just arriving now. We're calm, obviously aware that tomorrow will be a huge match for us, and we're all focused.

"It goes without saying that [Messis] is a great player, but what matters most to me is that the team realizes what is at stake: not just another trophy, but our consolidation as an institution. Beyond the chance to face a great player, the opportunity to win the title against a team like Inter Miami is about solidifying the work we've been doing and, above all, bringing joy to the fans."

Inter Miami currently sits in second place on the Eastern Conference table with 45 points in 25 games. The team has recorded just one victory in its last nine games.

Inter Miami forward Luis Suárez said he wants to use the game against Cruz Azul to start strong under new leadership.

"When it comes to playing a match like this, it's a final. There is no time to dwell on the past, the only thing that matters is looking ahead to tomorrow," Suárez said. "We've come through a challenging run of games, but now we face the best possible scenario: playing a final and moving forward with a new coach who brings great positive energy, a strong desire to grow and plenty of enthusiasm.

"That attitude is contagious, and we are ready to support him and his coaching staff."

Inter Miami hosts Cruz Azul before returning to Major League Soccer regular season action on Sunday against San Diego.

stories.headline: UFC's Islam Makhachev questions validity of Jon Jones' wins streak
stories.summary: UFC champ Islam Makhachev believes Jon Jones' failed drug tests and issues outside the Octagon invalidate Jones' place among the UFC's all-time streaks for consecutive wins.
stories.body:
Jon Jones and Islam Makhachev, two of the greatest fighters in UFC history, are taking shots at each other this week.

Makhachev (29-1) broke the UFC's official win streak record in August, when he defended his welterweight championship against Ian Machado Garry for his 17th consecutive win. Former middleweight champion Anderson Silva held the previous record of 16. Jones, a former light heavyweight and heavyweight champion, would argue he won 20 bouts in a row from 2010 to 2024, but his streak was interrupted by a no-contest against Daniel Cormier in 2017.

In a recent interview with a Russian news outlet, Makhachev said Jones' no-contest, which was the result of a failed drug test by the United States Anti-Doping Agency, invalidates his win streak.

"I'm not denying that Jon Jones is one of the greatest athletes in history, but he was caught doping twice," Makhachev told Ushatayka. "I think that's why his streak isn't considered valid. Because he went into a fight while on PEDs and won, that's where a new count should have started."

Jonse (28-1) was fined and suspended 15 months for testing positive for extremely trace amounts of steroid metabolites. He initially defeated Cormier in their fight in 2017, before it was later changed to a no-contest.

An independent arbitrator later stated he believed Jones unknowingly ingested the substance and that it was not performance enhancing. Jones has long pointed to that independent finding as validation of his innocence, and did so again Monday in a post directed at Makhachev.

"If you believe USADA for finding a picogram in my system, then you must believe USADA when they say it 'It was not found to be PERFORMANCE ENHANCING or INTENTIONAL,'" Jones wrote on X. "You can't have it both ways. Last I checked, my hand got raised every time I was in the Octagon since any of you can remember. Your own coach said I was 'a gift from God.' Let's not forget you've been KO'd, flatlined, went night night."

Makhachev, whose only loss came by knockout to Adriano Martins in his second UFC fight in 2015, responded to Jones the following day, and hinted at Jones's troubled legal history, both in and out of competition.

"Jon, I'm not trying to diminish your achievements in any way," Makhachev wrote on X. "But your whole life seems to be tied to breaking the rules one way or another, and somehow, you're never the one to be blamed."

stories.headline: Warriors sell out Eden Park in 48 hours amid NRL's crowd woes
stories.summary: Hooker Sam Healey plans to draw inspiration from his rugby league idol to help him handle the pulsating atmosphere of a sold-out Eden Park.
stories.body:
Hooker Sam Healey plans to draw inspiration from his NRL idol to help him handle the pulsating atmosphere of a sold-out Eden Park.

The NRL announced that general-public tickets for Sunday's do-or-die semi-final between the Warriors and Newcastle in Auckland had sold out in less than 48 hours.

It comes after New Zealand were forced to relocate from their traditional home ground for the clash because Eden Park hosts about 25,000 more spectators than Go Media Stadium.

The 50,000-seat venue being full comes after the league was criticised over poor crowd numbers in the first week of finals, although the Warriors had a mostly sold-out attendance for their 26-16 loss to the Dolphins.

Regardless, it's the club's first clash at Eden Park since 2014, and will be a mammoth moment for New Zealand rugby league as the Warriors look to keep alive their hopes of a first premiership.

Healey is yet to play at the venue, but will be wanting to produce similar heroics to his idol Kevin Locke, who made a courageous try-saving tackle on Sydney Roosters centre Michael Jennings at the Fortress in 2013.

"I have played league since I was five or six or something like that, so I always loved the game," Healey said.

"I actually saw him (Locke) in the sheds the other day, and I said to my mum, 'Do you remember when he was my favourite player'. She just started laughing.

"He used to be my lock-screen on my phone ... I just said g'day."

Warriors back-rower Jacob Laban has only played once at the country's biggest sporting stadium.

"It was Kiwi A's versus Tonga A's, I think it was two, three years ago," he said.

"(After) New Zealand played Samoa (in the Pacific Championships) ... it was a pretty cool, good atmosphere.

"Obviously it (the crowd) is a little bit further (away) than Mt Smart, but it's not too bad. When you score a try, you can walk up to the fans over there, so it's still pretty close."

Laban won't be intimidated by the history of Eden Park, although the club has won only one of its six games at the venue.

The blond second-rower is intent on not just helping the Warriors set up a preliminary final against Penrith, but also on making his childhood self proud.

"I knew I wanted to play for the Warriors when I first heard about rugby league," Laban said.

"They came to Wellington. I don't know what year it was, but I still have this photo of me where I had half a Warriors face painted on and a Warriors T-shirt.

"I knew I wanted to play for the Warriors since I was young."

stories.headline: Max vs 100: Can an amateur really beat Verstappen in a go-kart race?
stories.summary: ESPN's Nate Saunders is one of 100 amateur go-karters taking on four-time world champion Max Verstappen on Wednesday, live on Disney+. Here, he previews the event.
stories.body:
Ten seconds into the dress rehearsal for racing against Max Verstappen, the GoPro attached to the front of my kart had already been knocked clean off.

Up ahead, around and behind me, 49 other amateur racers were trying to squeeze through the first corner five abreast. Behind me was Formula 1 rookie and Red Bull junior Arvid Lindblad, playing the role of Verstappen for the afternoon's dress rehearsal and carving through the congestion at an alarming rate. Somewhere in the middle of all that was me, discovering that the first objective in taking on one of the greatest racing drivers of his generation is considerably less ambitious than beating him.

Objective one: Survive long enough for Verstappen to actually catch you at a meaningful moment, rather than just in a flash.

- How Verstappen's karting years made an F1 champion - and prepared him for an all-new test

- Max vs 100 explained: Rules, drivers, shortcuts and how Verstappen can win

- Max vs 100: F1 drivers predict how Verstappen will fare racing 100 drivers

On Wednesday, I will be one of 100 drivers attempting exactly that at Silverstone: Verstappen starts at the back and has 30 laps to pass 100 of us. The slightly absurd event will be broadcast live on Disney+, meaning there is an even more modest secondary ambition: remain in the contest long enough to make it onto television.

The obvious first question is how, and then, why is anyone getting the chance to do this? Both good starting points. Verstappen has taken on the challenge of racing 100 amateur karting drivers and beating them over 30 laps at a purpose-built kart track at Silverstone. The event is being broadcast live on Disney+, with build-up at 5 p.m. BST before the race begins at 6 p.m. It's very on-brand for Verstappen, who recently has made a point of taking on just about every racing challenge he can think of outside of Formula 1.

When asked what he is expecting from the event, Verstappen himself last week said: "Just seeing the carnage unfold in front of me."

He might not have to wait long. Red Bull staged a practice run on Tuesday, with the impressive Racing Bull youngster Lindblad standing in for Verstappen against two separate fields of 50 on the shorter track. Verstappen's race will take place on a mis-match of two different circuits: 1.3km of permanent karting track on the Silverstone infield, with another 1.15km of temporary track added specifically for this event. The rules for Lindblad's dress rehearsal were the same: start at the back, and once a driver is passed, they are eliminated. Drivers were given a handy 'fast lap' -- think a shortcut -- at one stage, for the first 50 percent of the race, while Lindblad had use of the same opportunity for the second 50 percent of the race. The same rules will apply for Verstappen in Wednesday's longer, one-hour event.

George Russell had jokingly suggested beforehand that the best defence might be to run four abreast and make Verstappen find a way through. By Turn 1 of the morning rehearsal, that had become five abreast without anyone appearing to have planned it. Starting 36th, Turn 1 was a warzone, and the GoPro was gone sooner than I could remember what any of the advice before had been. As it did go flying one way, there was a flash of white the other -- Lindblad, in his Racing Bulls gear, nimbly scything through the pack, inexplicably already some 10 or 15 places up, carving past karts which were spinning left, right and centre. Barely 10 seconds had passed and ESPN's dress rehearsal was over, as was a good quarter of the field's.

"You have to survive lap one," says David Terrien, the man who constructed the circuit for this event and will be race director. He's got a point: The 'fast lap' option only exists to drivers who make it round for one full lap, after all.

Terrien, a former European and World karting champion, raced against both of Verstappen's parents, Jos Verstappen and Sophie Kumpen, when they were kids together. He was given the task of creating a racetrack that did several things all at once: first, stuck to the highest safety standards required for such an event, second, to be long enough to accommodate a field of 100 cars, and three, to provide some genuine entertainment to the watching audience at home. "Max will gain quite a few positions at the start," Terrien said, even before Lindblad's dry run had offered obvious proof that would be the case. "But a karting field spreads out very quickly and it's not as easy as you might think to make progress. This track has been built like no other, as kart races never accommodate 100 karts like this. They also don't have such a mis-match of experience levels and talent." Light offence taken, there, but a fair shot.

Regardless of all that, though, surely Verstappen, one of the greatest drivers motor racing has ever seen, should make mincemeat of everyone. Right?

"I'm not so sure. It's very difficult, even for a driver of Max's calibre," Terrien said. "The field will be carnage early on but even the best karters would find progress difficult on a track such as this."

On Tuesday's dry run, Lindblad did not disappear into the distance. In fact, by the end of the race, he had ticked off 49 of the 50 karters he needed to catch. After roughly 15 minutes of flat-out racing, Red Bull athlete and streamer RDJavi was punching the air as he crossed the line metres ahead. Perhaps Lindblad was far too diplomatic in his pursuit of the victory. Versappen has already teased all-out war with the men and women sharing a race track with him.

"Oh, I'm not gonna be nice," he laughed at a question recently. "Actually, I asked Red Bull 'can I crash into them?'"

Verstappen might be using his in-helmet radio to broadcast some intimidating messages to the drivers he chasing. Asked what he might say to his rivals ahead of the Spanish Grand Prix, Verstappen laughed: "You better move out of the way, otherwise I'm going to plough them into the barrier. I was very serious. Like, you better move when I'm coming..."

Point taken. In me, he's not coming up against a pro. My karting experience, despite the profession in motor racing, might be limited to nine or 10 outings with friends and on stag do's. Hardly ideal preparation for a breathless race to not be overtaken by one of the best drivers Formula 1 has ever seen.

The benefit from Tuesday's track time might be limited. Fans who yearn for "the good old days" of Formula 1 will be thrilled to know the grid for the Verstappen event will be set after a one-shot qualifying lap; drivers will only do one lap of the full course before racing against him. "We did not want the competitors to have too unfair an advantage on Max, given that he's starting last," Terrien tells me, apparently without irony as he refers to a four-time world champion and a man many believe to be the most naturally gifted to have driven a Formula 1 car.

Verstappen's participation in the event is, in effect, a love letter to go-karting. Verstappen was a phenom in his junior career and his success fast-tracked him to Formula 1. "It was a really nice period in my life," Verstappen told ESPN recently about his karting days. His fondness is linked to the countless hours travelling with his father Jos around Europe. The pair estimate they clocked up 60,000 motorway miles a year together.

Win or lose, the mere fact Verstappen even wants to put his reputation on the line against 100 amateurs continues a recent trend at this end of his career. Last year, and this year, he turned to sports car racing and the 24 Hours of Nurburgring to seek the thrill of racing he was no longer getting from Formula 1.

Wednesday's race might not scratch the itch in the same way, and it certainly won't last for quite as long, but Verstappen is going to have his work cut out for him if he wants to avoid Lindblad's fate of watching another driver just stay ahead -- especially in front of a worldwide Disney+ audience.

stories.headline: Source: Chargers signing Valdes-Scantling to practice squad
stories.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers, depleted at receiver after a loss to the Arizona Cardinals, are signing Marquez Valdes-Scantling, 31, to its practice squad, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, adding a veteran who was a 2018 fifth-round choice from USF.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The Chargers are signing wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Tuesday.

Valdez-Scantling, 31, spent his first four seasons with the Green Bay Packers, then two with the Kansas City Chiefs. The veteran has also played for the Buffalo Bills, New Orleans Saints, San Francisco 49ers and Pittsburgh Steelers.

A fifth-round choice in 2018 out of South Florida, Valdez-Scantling spent training camp with the Dallas Cowboys, but the team released him when it cut its roster to 53 players.

Valdes-Scantling's signing comes after Sunday's loss to the Cardinals in which wide receivers Ladd McConkey (rib), KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) and Derius Davis (undisclosed) were injured. On Tuesday, the Chargers put Lambert-Smith on injured reserve, meaning he'll sit out at least four games.​

The Cardinals had no answer for McConkey on Sunday. He had five catches for 82 yards and looked as if he was on the way for much more. But in the third quarter, linebacker Mack Wilson Sr. delivered a big hit as McConkey attempted to make a leaping grab on an in-breaking route in the middle of the field. McConkey was on the ground in apparent significant pain before leaving the field. He didn't return.

Davis was injured on a Justin Herbert interception. Herbert launched a deep pass to Davis who was blanketed by two Cardinals defenders. As Davis attempted to make the grab, he landed awkwardly on his shoulder, and the ball was intercepted by safety Andrew Wingard. Davis returned to the game.

Also Tuesday, the Chargers signed wide receiver Gary Jennings to the active roster from the practice squad.

stories.headline: Anaheim Ducks sign Cutter Gauthier, 22, to six-year contract
stories.summary: After creating salary-cap space with the release of Chris Kreider, the Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday signed Cutter Gauthier to a six-year contract, with GM Pat Verbeek saying in a statement that the 22-year-old left wing is "a major part of our young core."
stories.body:
The Anaheim Ducks signed forward Cutter Gauthier, 22, to a six-year contract, the team announced Tuesday night. The deal is worth $13.5 million annually, sources told ESPN.

The contract includes an $18.6 million signing bonus plus $850,000 in salary in Year 1. So Gauthier will make nearly $19.5 million in his first year, a source said.

The agreement keeps one of Anaheim's young cornerstones in place after a breakout season in which Gauthier led the Ducks with 41 goals and 69 points. The Ducks exceeded expectations by making the playoffs last season and upsetting the Edmonton Oilers in the first round.

Gauthier, 22, scored 12 points in 12 playoff games for the Ducks in their first postseason appearance in eight years.

He was the No. 5 pick of the 2022 NHL draft by the Philadelphia Flyers. After arriving in Anaheim in a 2024 blockbuster trade, Gauthier became a restricted free agent this summer coming off his entry-level contract.

"This is a very exciting day for my family and I," Gauthier said in a team statement. "I'm so pleased to be able to sign long term with the Ducks and be part of what I believe is a great future."

The offseason has been transformative for Anaheim, which matched an offer sheet for Leo Carlsson from Philadelphia in July. That deal made Carlsson the NHL's highest-paid player at $18 million per season, which has now been surpassed twice -- by San Jose Sharks forward Macklin Celebrini and Colorado Avalanche defenseman Cale Makar.

The Carlsson contract and the impending deal for Gauthier forced the Ducks to waive veteran Chris Kreider last week for what general manager Pat Verbeek called "salary cap flexibility." Kreider went on to sign a one-year deal with the Montreal Canadiens and was introduced Monday.

Gauthier's deal came down on the final day of the NHL's old collective bargaining agreement, which allows for eight-year contract limits. That deadline spurred a flurry of deals around the league. Moving forward, a player can sign with his team for a maximum of seven years. Also new in the CBA, rules will change on how salary bonus money is structured -- which will limit front-loaded deals such as the one Anaheim gave Gauthier.

Gauthier, who was born in Sweden where is father was playing professionally, was raised in the United States. He progressed through the U.S. national team development program and Boston College, where he was a Hobey Baker Award finalist.

stories.headline: September Draft Power Rankings: An extended top 35, plus current player comparisons
stories.summary: The majority of top-age junior campaigns are now over, with prospects putting their best foot forward to show off for recruiters all season. Here's Jasper Chellappah's September Power Rankings, with an extended top 35 and player comparisons.
stories.body:
The majority of top-age campaigns are over, with prospects putting their best foot forward to show off for recruiters all season. Through club and state we've witnessed a draft class explode with depth across the year. 2026 offers a pool that runs 70 deep which clubs will be keen to take on in the national draft.

Jackson Phillips' Dandenong Stingrays will face Wil Malady's Gippsland Power in a south-west Victorian clash to decide the Coates Talent League premier. In WA, Heath Mellody and George Gale are into a WAFL Grand Final for Claremont against Peel.

Mellody headlines the movement in September's Power Rankings. His rise has come off the back of a brilliant stint at senior level after winning the Larke Medal at the National Championships. While not the favourite to be crowned pick one in the open draft he's amongst six named to still be in the most wide open race since Essendon last picked at the top in 2016.

With added player comparisons targeting the best traits of this year's prospects, this is ESPN's extended top 35 prospects in September for the AFL Draft.

Previous rankings: April | May | June | July | August | September

1. Dougie Cochrane (Port Adelaide NGA) (previously: 1)

Central District/South Australia

FWD/MID, 195cm

SANFL: 4 games, 17.8 disposals, 3.8 marks, 2.3 tackles

There was every chance Cochrane wouldn't play a game in his top-age season after undergoing patella surgery in the off-season. Instead we got to see him in a variety of roles for Port Adelaide's SANFL side late in the year with the athletic utility offering glimpses of class. He's been the 'pick 1 apparent' of his draft class since commanding performances at the U16s championships, backing it up with dominance beyond his years as a bottom-ager for club and state. Cochrane projects to become a key forward at the next level but holds ambitions of moving on-ball at 195cm. With Zak Butters pledging his future to the Western Bulldogs, Cochrane is all but assured of landing at Alberton.

Traits similar to: Charlie Curnow

2. Cody Walker (Carlton Father-son) (2)

Bendigo Pioneers/Vic Country

MID, 184cm

National Championships: 3 games, 23.7 disposals, 3.7 clearances, 1.3 tackles

Walker's stints with Carlton VFL cemented his status in this draft pool. He's an athletic talent around the ball with speed and balance allowing him to shark loose balls on the fly and exit the contest shoulders out and toward goal. Walker's kryptonite has continually been the ball use and decision making, often biting off too much or scrubbing kicks under pressure which puts his side on the back foot. There will be positional versatility in his game given the ball-winning quality and athletic tools, and he may need to hone his skills on the outside of the contest before graduating on-ball for the Blues.

Traits similar to: Chad Warner

3. Arki Butler (4)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID/FWD, 182cm

National Championships: 3 games, 12.3 disposals, 7.0 marks, 1.7 goals

Adversity hit Butler's airborne campaign with a broken collarbone during the National Championships. It put serious doubt into the remainder of his season but the goalsneak returned to captain Brighton Grammar to the first APS Grand Final win ever and put together an encouraging game on the weekend despite the Dragons losing out in a thrilling preliminary final. Butler has offered glimpses as a midfielder with his strength and acceleration -- attributes he can use to win his own ball, but he clearly projects as a powerful one-on-one goalkicker inside 50. The powerfully built teen is brilliant in the air, crafty at ground level and uses both feet around goals to pay full price. In a wide open race for the open pool No. 1 selection, Butler has his nose in front of a group of six.

Traits similar to: Toby Greene

READ: 'All damage' - Arki Butler is the 2026 draft's most watchable junior footballer

4. Heath Mellody (8)

Claremont/Western Australia

MID/DEF, 184cm

National Championships: 4 games, 28.2 disposals, 5.0 marks, 2.5 tackles

Mellody has been on the scene for 12 months. He ripped apart a Colts Grand Final from the wing as a bottom-ager and now gets his chance at a senior premiership with Claremont after a sparkling finish to his junior career. Mellody's second half of the season has been the best of anyone in the draft; the Larke Medallist was a shining light through the midfield for WA and didn't play a single Colts game before making his League debut in the final two rounds of the year.

Mellody has been a key piece of Claremont's run. He's been thrown around the ground including stints at half forward, halfback and on a wing, but his best football has come as a true centre bounce midfielder. He possesses an insatiable work ethic, hitting top speed to find space and commanding the football with his dogged determination to provide an option. He can win his own ball with clean hands under pressure but is at his best on the fly with eyes scanning inside 50. Mellody's ball use can be wayward as he tries to do too much at times, but he offers lovely technique and it has been a strength of his through junior football before his move into the midfield. He plays above his size with strong hands in the air which we saw off halfback last year and can get forward to hit the scoreboard bursting inside 50. This six-game stretch at senior level after winning the Larke Medal will see Mellody drafted as the highest WA prospect since Luke Jackson, and could even see him taken as the top pick in the open pool. He is 2026's draft bolter and could rise all the way to the pinnacle this year.

Traits similar to: Lachie Ash

THE PICK 1 PIE: Who is in the running to be taken first from the open pool?

5. Harry Van Hattum (3)

Northern Knights/Vic Metro

RUC/FWD, 205cm

National Championships: 4 games, 10.8 disposals, 2.5 marks, 22.0 hitouts

Few rucks possess the combination of traits Van Hattum is blessed with. A genuine ruck size with a top-heavy frame relied upon for his aggressive nature, the Knights star is an elite kick and strong presence at stoppages. If he isn't claiming the ball from ruck contests himself he's buttering up with craft in the clinches, getting on the burst to receive handballs and executing with ball use inside 50. He can get his contested marking game going around the ground and offers genuine presence as a target inside 50. Van Hattum's limitations come in his consistent efforts and fitness to spread from contests and run out games. He is clearly hampered by his tank and will need to become a strong runner in time to make it as an AFL ruckman because it doesn't come naturally to him.

Traits similar to: Brodie Grundy

READ: 'I just hate that' - Harry Van Hattum wants to end ruck disrespect

6. Ethan Drever (6)

GWV Rebels/Vic Country

MID, 188cm

National Championships: 4 games, 20.0 disposals, 4.5 marks, 4.2 tackles

No one stops Drever on the burst out of a contest. The flying Rebel is at his very best on the move around stoppage, collecting loose balls and creating separation with a long striding gait entering the 50. He's an excellent defensive presence at stoppage, willing to dig in to chase down opponents, apply physical pressure at the drop of the ball and run hard in defensive transition. That separates him from a lot of the very best midfielders to come through the junior pathways. Drever's consistency has been a point of contention for draft watchers, fluctuating in both his impact on the game and his skill execution by foot. He can be haphazard in his ball use forward of centre which holds Drever back from being the most damaging player in the pool.

Traits similar to: Finn Callaghan

7. Gus Teixeira (5)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID, 181cm

National Championships: 4 games, 17.0 disposals, 4.2 tackles, 1.8 goals

Teixeira plays with authority. The Dragons star has split time through the midfield and up forward through a breakout top-age season, but there remain doubts over whether he cracks it as an inside midfielder at the senior level. Teixeira is powerful with ball in hand, creates space for himself efficiently and executes well by hand and foot. He's a threat around goals and has the speed to play off half forward at the next level, but doesn't play through contact well and isn't the cleanest player in the draft below his knees. He projects to become an excellent forward that can pinch hit through the middle but may lack the natural midfield craft to operate in the engine room full-time.

Traits similar to: Jordan De Goey

8. Mitch Harris (12)

Woodville-West Torrens/South Australia

DEF, 195cm

National Championships: 4 games, 8.8 disposals, 3.5 marks, 1.0 tackles

There isn't a more intimidating aerial presence in the draft than Harris. A genuine contested marking threat at either end of the ground, he's honed his craft down back as a lockdown option and produced a stellar carnival to stake his claims as a top 10 pick. Harris does his work early and establishes position with his physicality, but also has a good vertical leap to come over the top of packs. He's offered glimpses of upside as a forward but will be drafted as a lockdown key defender.

Traits similar to: Sam Collins

9. Ethan Matthews (Giants Academy) (9)

Giants Academy/Allies

MID, 186cm

National Championships: 2 games, 25.0 disposals, 5.0 marks, 6.0 tackles

Matthews is an excellent midfield prospect that will find his way to the Giants via their academy. He's a ball magnet, clean and clinical with his use but not as damaging as others at the top of the pool in his willingness to take the game on and exit stoppage forward of centre. There's scope for Matthews to play through the midfield, off a wing or on halfback with his cleanliness, running power and reliability.

Traits similar to: Sam Flanders

10. Wil Malady (10)

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

FWD, 190cm

National Championships: 3 games, 10.7 disposals, 5.7 marks, 1.3 goals

Malady is one of the best athletes this year, a powerful runner with high top-end speed mixed in with a ridiculous vertical leap. His spring gives him a chance to fly for every ball kicked his way and his dogged running patterns put him in the best position to impact ahead of the ball. It's an unsexy pick to target third tall forwards at this stage of the draft but Malady offers match-winning traits with reliability in his role at the next level.

Traits similar to: Ollie Henry

11. Clancy Snell (7)

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

DEF, 196cm

National Championships: 4 games, 13.0 disposals, 7.0 marks, 2.5 tackles

Snell reads the play superbly and backs himself always. He's an interceptor first and foremost, relying on his superior reach, closing speed and reading of the ball in flight to pluck marks and kickstart transition. He can give up a long leash on direct opponents and get caught out by quick ball movement, but he's also shown off strong one-on-one play that gives scope for him to be a reliable lockdown defender in time.

Traits similar to: Josh Worrell

12. Khaled El Souki (Western Bulldogs NGA) (11)

FWD, 174cm

National Championships: 1 game, 10.0 disposals, 5.0 tackles, 1.0 goals

El Souki may be the hardest player to tackle in the draft. With his short stature, power through the hips and willingness to twist and turn out of danger, the Jets forward has been a goalkicking machine all season and gives defenders headaches with his activity around the ball. He's elite in forward stoppages with craft and confidence, and has shown glimpses of genuine midfield minutes if he can build his tank.

Traits similar to: Kysaiah Pickett

13. Sam Gayfer (13)

Northern Knights/Vic Metro

FWD, 194cm

National Championships: 4 games, 11.0 disposals, 4.2 marks, 2.5 goals

The vertical leap and aggression of Gayfer through the air is a joy to watch, crashing packs and exerting his presence consistently through games. His big carnival vaulted him up the rankings but he's also a willing defensive presence with the speed and aggression to chase down opponents. At the very minimum Gayfer will be an excellent role player with his capacity to bring the ball to ground and impact at his size.

Traits similar to: Mitch Georgiades

14. Leo Steed (17)

Swan Districts/Western Australia

MID, 176cm

National Championships: 4 games, 23.5 disposals, 3.0 marks, 4.0 tackles

Steed will be a fan favourite at the next level with a bucket of courage and bravery as a smaller midfielder. He accepts contact and plays through physicality, working himself into the ground to win his own ball and get it going forward. He's become a much better kick this year and, while still not a strength, found a role at senior level by hitting the scoreboard and setting up teammates inside 50. There's traits that will allow Steed to thrive as a midfielder at the next level if he can overcome middling athleticism.

Traits similar to: Caleb Serong

15. Jake Eime (18)

Central District/South Australia

DEF, 182cm

National Championships: 4 games, 20.2 disposals, 3.8 marks, 1.2 tackles

As a pure role player, there are few better halfback prospects to come through the junior ranks in some years. Eime is an elite athlete with the confidence to take the game on. He thrives in transition where he can motor along a wing and link the chains, though often will take on the riskier kick and back himself to execute, sometimes to the detriment of the team. Eime has the chops to lockdown on smalls, can play above his size in the air and loves to get forward and be damaging.

Traits similar to: Darcy Wilmot

16. Harrison Chapman (14)

Eastern Ranges/Vic Metro

MID, 190cm

National Championships: 3 games, 18.7 disposals, 4.7 marks, 2.0 tackles

There's something to unlock in Chapman's game at the next level. With his height and length he shouldn't be as natural below his knees and with ball in hand, expertly crafting attacking forays through the middle of the ground with multiple disposals in passages. He's a lovely quick and truly elite runner which gives him a chance of being an excellent wing at the next level, but it's the inside midfield upside that has clubs keen in the first round.

Traits similar to: Will Day

17. Caylen Murray (Lions Academy) (19)

Lions Academy/Allies

DEF/MID, 183cm

National Championships: 4 games, 24.0 disposals, 6.8 marks, 1.8 tackles

Murray is another in the line of excellent Lions academy prospects. One of the best ball users in the draft, he's willing to take on the kicks through the corridor but is equally adept at retaining possession and moving the ball methodically. Murray hasn't quite proved his midfield credentials but will become a reliable halfback quickly.

Traits similar to: Lachie Whitfield

18. Ethan Herbert (15)

North Adelaide/South Australia

RUC/FWD, 200cm

National Championships: 4 games, 15.8 disposals, 3.0 marks, 2.5 tackles

Herbert is a rare ruck archetype, with elite stoppage craft and the aerobic capacity to work opponents into the ground and win the ball on the outside. He's been a work in progress as a forward and some recruiters suggest he may be better suited to a key defence post where he can intercept, but there's untapped potential in what Herbert can produce at a genuine ruck size.

Traits similar to: Tim English

19. Kodah Edwards (16)

South Adelaide/South Australia

MID, 183cm

National Championships: 4 games, 22.0 disposals, 4.5 marks, 3.2 tackles

Edwards is unique in this draft. He's an inside midfielder in the older fashion of tough, bullocking prospects. But he's also got an X-factor to his game in the forward 50, thriving in one-on-ones and kicking goals by the bunch if given open space to work with. His limitations include ball use and decision making but his excellent hands and upside as a forward target gives him a chance of landing in the first round.

Traits similar to: Matt Kennedy

20. Tyson Bradley (20)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

DEF, 195cm

National Championships: 4 games, 14.5 disposals, 6.5 marks, 1.0 tackles

Bradley is the third of a group of key defenders who could land in the first round. The Vic Metro MVP and captain of the Sandringham Dragons is a neat ball user and can act as a distributor out of defence, plus reads the play well to operate as a sweeper behind the ball. Bradley ticks a lot of boxes for clubs in the market for a key defender around this point of the draft.

Traits similar to: Jordan Ridley

21. Noah Williams (21)

Geelong Falcons/Vic Country

MID, 177cm

National Championships: 4 games, 15.5 disposals, 4.0 marks, 5.8 tackles

There's no questioning Williams' endeavour and desperation. He's a maniacal presence at the coalface and looks at home on-ball since a move from halfback in the pre-season. Unfortunately it's been a season full of niggles and inconsistencies, and recruiters don't see the weapons that other midfielders possess at the top of the pool.

Traits similar to: Tom Atkins

22. Marlon Neocleous (28)

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

FWD/MID, 168cm

National Championships: 2 games, 16.0 disposals, 5.0 marks, 0.5 goals

It's been a strong finish to the season for Neocleous, who no doubt is a very different prospect to others around him. A natural goal sneak, he loves the ball in his hands up afield and is at his best with some space to execute in the forward half. He's an adept crumber and finisher in the forward 50, but lacks the pace to separate from opponents and doesn't have the tricks to exit congestion like some others.

Traits similar to: Jack Higgins

23. Jack Pickett (24)

Geelong Falcons/Vic Country

FWD, 194cm

Pickett was a top prospect throughout his bottom-age campaign. He's a traditional key forward that presents full-chested at the kicker and marks with arms outstretched. He's also a lovely set shot for goal, but is rehabilitating a torn ACL this year.

Traits similar to: Jye Amiss

24. Gabe Patterson (27)

Glenelg/South Australia

FWD, 184cm

National Championships: 4 games, 13.0 disposals, 2.5 tackles, 1.0 goals

After a tough championships it's been a truly brilliant second half of the season for Patterson. There's little doubt over the forward's impact with ball in hand, but finding enough of it has been a concern and showcasing his power and athleticism often enough has been something for Patterson to build towards. He's given recruiters something to think about towards the first round of the draft after blistering form in front of goals.

Traits similar to: Beau McCreery

25. Harvie Cooke (22)

Northern Knights/Vic Metro

MID/FWD, 176cm

National Championships: 4 games, 17.5 disposals, 7.0 marks, 1.0 goals

Cooke is 2026's Morrish Medallist for best and fairest in the Coates Talent League. It's well deserved for the midfielder's excellent season at the Knights where he was roving to Van Hattum and hitting the scoreboard regularly. Cooke was forced into forward roles at Metro where he was equally as damaging and showed he didn't need midfield minutes to create space for himself and hurt the opposition by foot.

Traits similar to: Sam Switkowski

26. Koby LeCras (26)

West Perth/Western Australia

FWD/MID, 192cm

A best on ground performance for the AFL Academy sits firmly in the minds for all draft watchers despite LeCras partially tearing his ACL and sitting out the rest of the year. The nephew of West Coast's Mark is a taller but equally creative half forward who can roam up onto a wing with his engine. He's clinical and efficient in his disposals.

Traits similar to: Ollie Dempsey

27. Jackson Phillips (-)

Dandenong Stingrays/Vic Country

MID, 182cm

National Championships: 4 games, 16.2 disposals, 3.8 marks, 3.2 tackles

Phillips's Stingrays are grand final bound, aided by his excellent midfield play. He offers impact with every possession, not collecting huge numbers but getting the ball in dangerous spots and regularly hitting the scoreboard. He likely doesn't exhibit the tools to be a bona fide inside midfielder at the next level but has positional versatility in his ball use and running power and could play off a wing or half forward.

Traits similar to: Justin McInerny

28. Toby Krasna (28)

Northern Knights/Vic Metro

MID, 181cm

National Championships: 3 games, 19.0 disposals, 3.3 marks, 1.0 goals

Krasna does his best work in transition where he finds space and excels kicking inside 50. He won't be a centre bounce midfielder at the next level without winning more of his own ball and averaged under one clearance per game for Vic Metro, but he's a standout prospect with the ball in the forward half.

Traits similar to: Jake Soligo

29. Keenan Boi (-)

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

FWD, 180cm

National Championships: 3 games, 13.3 disposals, 4.7 marks, 1.0 goals

Boi plays with rare physicality for junior football, bodylining the ball and man and exerting his authority with an edge. He's clean and executes under pressure when he needs to but brings his best traits forward without the ball where he tackles and pressures with the best of small forwards. He's primed for a big grand final on the weekend.

Traits similar to: Sam Powell-Pepper

30. George Dimer (23)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

FWD, 173cm

National Championships: 3 games, 16.0 disposals, 5.7 marks, 1.0 goals

Dimer is an intelligent small forward with the runs on the board for clubs to be confident that he won't be held back by his size. His performances for Haileybury in the APS were undeniable, plus he was one of Vic Metro's better forwards throughout the carnival despite not being a focal point in attack. He crumbs well, uses the ball smartly and creates opportunities for others.

Traits similar to: Hussien El Achkar

31. Albert MacGowan (-)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID, 187cm

National Championships: 4 games, 22.8 disposals, 6.2 marks, 1.0 tackles

One of the hottest players to finish the year has been MacGowan, who ended the year with a bang as the Dragons best performed player. He has operated with great success off a wing thanks to his aerial presence and skills, but has ambitions of becoming an inside midfielder if he can add ball-winning to his repertoire. MacGowan's knack of hitting the scoreboard with lovely set shots would be a nice penchant to transition to senior level.

Traits similar to: Matt Johnson

32. Marcus Prasad (-)

Dandenong Stingrays

FWD/MID, 167cm

Prasad is undersized and hasn't demonstrated midfield craft to the level you'd be confident projecting it. It's his forward half craft that makes him a national draft candidate, supremely gifted below his knees to the point he may be the cleanest player in the draft. Prasad gathers and swivels like lightning, though lacks penetration in his kick and doesn't hit the scoreboard to the regularity of other half forwards.

Traits similar to: Arthur Jones

33. Lochie Burrows (-)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

DEF/MID, 181cm

National Championships: 4 games, 13.0 disposals, 4.8 marks, 1.8 tackles

Burrows is brave and bold, with a blonde shock of hair you can't miss and endeavour at the coalface. He's played some of his best football as a hard-nosed midfielder with an appetite to tackle and pressure, but he appeals to clubs down back where he can lock down and intercept with good hands in the air.

Traits similar to: Max Michalanney

34. Benji Van Rooyen (30)

Claremont/Western Australia

RUC, 203cm

National Championships: 4 games, 14.0 disposals, 4.0 marks, 20.5 hitouts

Van Rooyen was the best performing ruck at the carnival, and deserves consideration higher than this mark. He showed off strong positioning behind the ball in open play to mop up for WA countless times and he doesn't overuse the ball. There's scope for Van Rooyen to play forward at his size but his ruck craft has steadily improved this year.

Traits similar to: Darcy Cameron

35. George Gale (29)

Claremont/Western Australia

MID, 190cm

National Championships: 4 games, 27.8 disposals, 5.2 marks, 2.8 tackles

Gale will play in a senior grand final this weekend after a stellar finish to the year. He burst into top 30 calculations with a strong showing at the carnival for WA and his power running through midfield is a feature. Gale could be an excellent wing at the next level with his positioning and strength lending himself to auxiliary roles, but he's also shown quality as an inside midfielder.

Traits similar to: Bo Allan

stories.headline: Paul George ready to prove self in wake of controversial trade
stories.summary: Paul George acknowledged Celtics fans' angst toward the trade that sent Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia for him, saying it's understandable.
stories.body:
BOSTON -- Paul George made one thing clear during his introductory news conference with the Boston Celtics on Tuesday: His ears work just fine.

He has heard the not-so-silent chorus of Celtics fans who bemoaned the front office's decision to jettison 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown in the July trade with Philadelphia that sent George to his fifth NBA team.

But George, 36, also isn't shying away from his new situation.

"I understand my circumstances. I understand how huge JB was, not only for the organization but here in the city. So I didn't take it personal," George said. "To be honest, they should have a relationship, emotionally, to that trade.

"But my job is to kind of come into a great opportunity for me. Obviously, the last few years have been rough, just with injuries. But for myself personally, I feel great again. I feel like I've turned that corner of dealing with injuries and now kind of reestablishing myself from a physical standpoint again. And with that, I can carry it over to the court."

George, along with acquisitions Mitchell Robinson and Mike Conley, represent president of basketball operations Brad Stevens' attempt to shore up the roster alongside Jayson Tatum.

The franchise centerpiece, Tatum is embarking on his first full season since tearing an Achilles tendon in May 2025 and then having his return late last season end with him being sidelined for the Celtics' Game 7 first-round playoff loss to George and the 76ers.

Robinson comes in fresh off winning a championship with the Knicks, and Conley will be suiting up with his fourth NBA team as he prepares for his 20th season.

Robinson missed Tuesday's news conference for a personal matter, but Stevens said likes what he has seen over the past few weeks during workouts between the three newcomers and returning members of Boston's roster as they prepare to open training camp in two weeks.

The trio also joined Tatum and other current Celtics for informal workouts this summer.

The team held its annual season launch event Monday and Stevens said there was only one image behind him when he spoke to everyone -- a photo of the TD Garden court being refurbished.

"That happens every year right around the end of July. And to me, every single year you go through it looks like the blank canvas of a court being absolutely redone," Stevens said. "Nobody's stepped on it. And now it's that year's team. To write its own chapter. And I felt that way every time they do it."

Characterized as a facelift or a complete renovation, the key players of the Celtics teams that hoisted the franchise's 18th title in 2024 have changed over the summer.

Whether those alterations wind up paying off will depend on what this new trio -- and particularly George -- can provide at this stage of their careers.

Conley, 38, will be a role player behind Derrick White and Payton Pritchard, with Robinson likely backing up starting center Neemias Queta.

But for a player such as George, who has nine All-Star and six All-NBA selections, expectations are higher as he looks to step into the role of Tatum's tag team partner in the starting lineup.

Conley insisted he's "still got a lot left" and thinks two things he and George bring on day one are leadership and instant motivation to produce.

"It's two guys who haven't had a chance to win a championship," Conley said. "So, it's that sense of urgency that maybe reignites that for the guys who've been on this team, who've already won it."

George reiterated several times that a run of injuries he had with the LA Clippers and Sixers, including knee surgery prior to last season, are in the rearview and that he is a "great" place physically and mentally.

"It's a new group, a new opportunity," George said. "I think they're getting someone that's ready to, not fill the shoes or fill the void of JB, but I think from a personal standpoint myself, I think I can come in and kind of still keep us in that contention. Give us a chance to win."

Real Salt Lake and United States attacking midfielder Diego Luna is expected to be out for months and will likely undergo an arthroscopic procedure to determine the extent of a knee injury, sources confirmed to ESPN.

Luna, 23, is now set to miss not only a crucial part of the 2026 MLS season, but also the next call up for the U.S. men's national team.

The U.S. will face Peru, Chile, Mexico, and Canada in friendlies in late September through early October, in what will be the first games of a new World Cup cycle for coach Mauricio Pochettino.

stories.headline: Small changes in biggest weight class in MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
The UFC's heavyweight division appears to be stuck in neutral gear.

It's not just about Tom Aspinall vacating the championship on Monday because he is still recovering from an eye injury suffered in last October's no-contest in a title defense against Ciryl Gane. Gane, who won the interim championship with a knockout of Alex Pereira in June, remains atop the ESPN rankings. The top 10 still features Aspinall -- he's eligible to be ranked until the middle of next month, when he will have been inactive for a year -- and includes two heavyweights from outside the UFC in the top six (Francis Ngannou, Vadim Nemkov).

The heavyweight rankings underwent small changes as a result of Saturday's UFC matchup of top-10 fighters Waldo Cortes Acosta and Curtis Blaydes. Cortes Acosta entered the weekend ranked sixth, but after losing by unanimous decision, he drops to No. 9. Blaydes is one spot above him, moving up from 10th.

The only other movement in the divisional rankings is at women's flyweight, where former UFC champion Alexa Grasso moves up one position to No. 4 after Saturday's unanimous decision win over Manon Fiorot. Formerly ranked second, Fiorot drops three spots after her first loss in a nontitle bout since her pro debut in 2018.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.

stories.headline: Allianz Arena to host 2028 Champions League final, Camp Nou to host in 2029
stories.summary: The Munich Football Arena and Barcelona's Spotify Camp Nou will host the 2028 and 2029 UEFA Champions League finals, European football's governing body confirmed Tuesday.
stories.body:
The Munich Football Arena and Barcelona's Spotify Camp Nou will host the 2028 and 2029 UEFA Champions League finals, European football's governing body confirmed Tuesday.

Bayern Munich's stadium -- also known as the Allianz Arena for sponsorship reasons -- held the 2025 and 2012 finals, but it will be the first time in exactly 30 years that Camp Nou has been the venue for the biggest game in European club football.

Camp Nou last hosted the final in 1999, when Manchester United famously scored two late goals to beat Bayern 2-1 to claim the second of their three European Cups.

While the 70,000-capacity Allianz Arena is ready to go, Camp Nou is still being redeveloped as part of a revamp which began in 2023.

After over two years playing away from their home stadium, Barça returned to Camp Nou last November, but work is still ongoing.

The capacity is currently capped at 62,000, with the third tier yet to be completed and the roof still to be put on.

Barça estimate that the stadium, which will eventually hold 105,000 fans, will be finished towards the end of 2027 -- or at the latest by 2028.

- 2026 Ballon d'Or: Full men's, women's short lists, host city change, more

- Ousmane Dembélé: 'Never the chosen one,' but hard work at 'back of the class' earned Ballon d'Or

This season's Champions League final will be played at Atlético Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium.

There was also confirmation Tuesday that the Parc Olympic Lyonnais and the National Stadium of Wales in Cardiff will host the 2028 and 2029 UEFA Women's Champions League finals, respectively.

Meanwhile, the 2028 and 2029 UEFA Europa League finals will be played at the National Arena in Bucharest and the National Stadium Serbia in Belgrade.

The UEFA Conference League showpieces in the same years will take place at Juventus Stadium in Turin and the Puskás Aréna in Budapest.

Finally, the 2027 UEFA Super Cup with be played at the Johan Cruyff Arena in Amsterdam and the 2028 edition will be hosted by the Astana Arena in Astana.

stories.headline: Roosters make Walker call as half's absence laid bare
stories.summary: James Tedesco says Daly Cherry-Evans took ownership of his off night against Penrith, as the Sydney Roosters aim to knock Cronulla out of the finals.
stories.body:
James Tedesco claims it would be unfair to lay the blame for the Sydney Roosters' last-gasp finals loss to Penrith at the feet of veteran halfback Daly Cherry-Evans.

As the Roosters resisted the urge to rush Sam Walker back for Saturday's sudden-death semi-final with Cronulla, Tedesco revealed how Cherry-Evans had shouldered the blame for last Sunday's 19-12 defeat to the Panthers.

Cherry-Evans gave away a seven-tackle set in the final 10 minutes with Penrith halfback Nathan Cleary converting a field goal soon afterwards.

The 37-year-old Cherry-Evans then sprayed his own attempt wide when his side needed him to stay calm under pressure, which sent the Roosters into a sudden-death final against the Sharks.

"Straight away he accepted it, and as a team, you don't dump that all on him," Tedesco said.

"He's done that numerous times earlier in the year and nailed it in getting us where we needed to.

"But with Chez, with his experience and how comfortable he is in those situations, we have full confidence in whatever he decides to do.

"We know he's kicked a lot, but he's missed a few as well.

"I think with Chez's experience and his age, you can't hold on to those things. I think that's important for all of us."

Walker, meanwhile, has been left on ice for a further week after coach Trent Robinson had hinted the Queensland No. 7 was an outside chance of returning against Cronulla.

The 24-year-old Walker underwent ankle surgery after suffering a syndesmosis in a loss to the Dolphins last month.

"It's only been a couple of weeks, so he's probably got another week or so I'm guessing," Tedesco said.

"But he started to do some running, which is really quick after surgery, so we'll just see how he goes in progressing to give himself a chance."

Walker's absence means the Roosters will again be without one of their most dynamic threats when they face the Sharks with Robinson forced to rely on the relatively untested partnership of Cherry-Evans and Hugo Savala.

With the first-choice halves pairing of Walker and Cherry-Evans, the Roosters have scored at a tick over 26 points per game this season.

But with Savala and Cherry-Evans as a playmaking duo, Robinson's sides are scoring an average of just 16 points per game across three fixtures.

"He (Savala) has done his job and that's all we can ask, and that's why we love playing with him," Tedesco said.

"He'll do whatever it takes for the team, we love him as a person, as a player, and he's only going to keep getting better.

"I thought he was awesome. He'll be disappointed with some moments that he didn't nail, but overall, he's excited to get on the job this Saturday and play his part."

Back-rower Angus Crichton, who was a late scratching against Penrith, has been named in jersey No.17 by Robinson.
